transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess… it’s this memorial for my brother. It started as something small, but I’ve been spending most days on it now—calling people, finding songs, planning displays, even trips. My wife says I’ve let the garden and my walking group and all that slide. So… that’s why I’m here, I suppose.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your garden or walking group?

Yeah… I suppose I have. I haven’t been going to my walking group or book club much. The garden’s gotten away from me too.

It’s just… everything seems to end up being about the memorial display. Some people at the senior center got upset with me over it. My wife says most days are spent trying to calm me down or stop me from making another call or planning some trip or getting into an argument.
Have you been feeling unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable lately?

I guess… yes, sometimes. I get this feeling like I’m lit up, like I’ve got a real purpose and everyone’s finally going to understand what my family went through.

But then if my wife, or someone at the senior center, questions it or slows me down… I can snap. I don’t like admitting that, but yes.
Have you been more active or driven to accomplish goals in areas other than the memorial planning, like taking on new projects, working more, or starting other activities?

Not really other things, no. It’s mostly been the memorial.

I mean… it started small, but I’ve been spending most days on it now—calling people, finding songs, planning the display, even thinking about trips for it. And I guess that’s pushed the garden and walking group aside. My wife says it’s taken over.
Have you had any periods where you felt so good, so confident, or so full of energy that you felt you could do anything, even things that might seem unrealistic to others?

Yes… I suppose I have.

There are times I feel sort of lit up, like I’ve got this purpose and the whole town is finally going to understand what happened to our family. And then if my wife or someone at the senior center questions the display or tries to slow me down, I… I snap. I don’t like that part.
Have you had a period lasting several days where your mood was consistently elevated, overly good, or irritable, not just moments here and there?

Yes… for a few days at a time, I think.

It’s not just a quick mood. I’ll feel lit up, like there’s a real purpose to it all, and then if my wife or someone at the senior center questions things or slows me down, I get irritable… snap at them. I don’t like saying that, but yes.
Have you had a period where you felt this way for a week or more straight, without a break, where you were really high, overly energetic, or irritable most of the time?
Yes… I think so. It’s been going on, off and on but mostly there, for about two months now… since my brother passed and I started working on the tribute.

Can you tell me more about how long these periods of feeling 'lit up' or irritable usually last? Specifically, have there been times when this lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week straight?
Yes… I’d say it’s been most days. It’s hard to pin down exactly, but this has been going on about two months now, since my brother passed and I started working on the tribute.
Can you think of a specific time when you felt this way—'lit up' or irritable—for a full week without a break? If so, can you describe how that felt and what you were doing during that time?

Yeah… there was a stretch like that.

I was working on the display, the tribute. I felt… lit up, I guess. Like it really mattered, like the whole town was finally going to understand our family. I’d get going on it and didn’t want anyone stopping me.

And then if my wife said I was doing too much, or someone at the senior center questioned it, I’d snap. I didn’t mean to, but I’d get irritated fast. It felt like they were getting in the way.
Can you confirm if there was a time when you felt this way—'lit up' or irritable—every day for at least a full week without a break?

Yes… yes, there was. I felt lit up and full of purpose most of the time, like the whole town was finally going to understand our family. And if my wife, or someone at the senior center, slowed me down or questioned the display, I’d snap. It was… pretty much every day for that week.
Was there a time when you felt 'lit up' or irritable every day, all day, for at least one full week without any break in how you were feeling?

Yes. For that week, it was pretty much all the time. I felt lit up… full of purpose, like this display was going to make people finally understand our family.

And then if my wife or someone at the senior center questioned it or slowed me down, I’d snap. I didn’t really come down from it during that stretch.

During that week when you felt 'lit up' or irritable all the time, did you also notice that you were much more active or driven to get things done — like making calls, planning, or working on the memorial display — more than you usually would be?

Yeah… I was doing more than usual.

I couldn’t really sit in my chair like I normally do. I was up hauling boxes, making calls, moving papers around… going room to room. It felt like my body had more steam in it than a man my age ought to have.

During that time when you felt 'lit up' and were working a lot on the memorial, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual—like you could get by with only a few hours of sleep and still feel full of energy?
I’m not sure. I mean… I was up late some nights with all of it, but I don’t really know if I needed less sleep like that. I wasn’t keeping track.

During that time when you felt 'lit up' and were working a lot on the memorial, did you find that you could get by with less sleep than usual—like only a few hours a night and still feel full of energy?
I don’t really know. I was up late, sure, but I can’t say I was only sleeping a few hours and feeling fine. I wasn’t paying that close attention.

During that time when you felt 'lit up' and were working a lot on the memorial, did you notice that you actually needed less sleep — like you could get by with only a few hours of sleep and still feel full of energy?
I can’t really say that, no. I was awake at odd hours, but whether I needed less sleep… I don’t know. I didn’t keep track of it like that.
Was there a time when you felt 'lit up' or irritable every day, all day, for at least one full week without any break in how you were feeling?

I don’t know if it was every day, all day like that. There were times I felt… lit up, full of purpose about it, like people were finally going to understand our family. And then I’d get irritated fast if my wife or someone at the senior center slowed me down or questioned the display.
Was there a specific time when you felt 'lit up' or irritable every day, all day, for at least one full week without any break in how you were feeling?

I don’t know about every day, all day, no breaks. It was more like… I’d feel lit up, like the whole town was finally going to understand our family, and then if my wife or someone at the senior center slowed me down or questioned the display, I’d snap. But I can’t say it was constant like that for a whole week.
Can you think of a time when you felt 'lit up' or irritable for at least 4 days in a row without a break in how you were feeling?

Maybe… I’m not sure about four days straight. It would come on where I felt lit up, like I had a purpose and the town was finally going to understand our family. Then if my wife, or someone at the senior center, slowed me down or questioned the display, I’d snap. But I don’t know if it was without a break.
Can you recall a time when you felt 'lit up' or irritable for at least 4 days in a row without a break in how you were feeling?

I’ve said, I’m not sure about the four days part. I do get… lit up, full of purpose, like the whole town’s finally going to understand our family. Then if my wife or someone at the senior center slows me down or questions the display, I snap. But I can’t say for sure it was four days straight without a break.
Can you recall if there was a time when you felt 'lit up' or irritable for 4 days in a row without a break in how you were feeling?

I don’t know about four days with no break. I just know I get lit up, like there’s a purpose to it, like people are finally going to understand our family. And then if my wife or somebody at the senior center slows me down or questions the display, I… I snap.
